menu_options.icloud: iCloud account (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods)
menu_options.network: Find My network account (AirTags and accessories)

icloud.title: iCloud account
icloud.description: Sign in with the Apple Account whose devices you want to follow.

data_description.with_family: Also add the devices of the family members who share their location with you

icloud_code.title: Verification code
icloud_code.description: Enter the verification code Apple sent to your trusted Apple devices or by text message. Home Assistant then becomes a trusted session and is not asked again.

network.title: Find My network account
network.description: Sign in with the Apple Account the accessories belong to. Their location reports are fetched from the Find My network.

advanced.name: Advanced options
advanced.description: Apple only answers clients that send anisette data. It is generated here by default; give the address of your own anisette server to use it instead.

data_description.anisette_url: For example http://192.168.1.10:6969, empty to generate it here

network_method.title: Verification method
network_method.description: How should Apple send the verification code?

network_code.title: Verification code
network_code.description: Enter the verification code shown on your trusted Apple devices.

network_sms_code.title: Verification code
network_sms_code.description: Enter the verification code sent by text message to {phone}.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: iCloud asks {account} to sign in again. Enter the password; a verification code may follow.

error.apple_refused: Apple refused the sign-in: “{reason}”. If the Apple Account and password are right, wait a few minutes and try again, or set an anisette server under Advanced options.
error.cannot_connect: Apple could not be reached. Try again in a few minutes.
error.anisette_error: Signing in failed: check that the anisette server answers, or leave it empty.
error.code_not_sent: Apple did not send a verification code. Try again in a few minutes.
error.no_second_factor: This Apple Account has no trusted device or phone number to receive a verification code.
error.security_key: This Apple Account signs in with a security key, which is not supported. Use an account with verification codes.

abort.code_not_sent: Apple did not send a verification code. Try again in a few minutes.
abort.wrong_account: This is not the account of this entry: sign in with the same Apple Account.

user.title: Add accessories
user.description: The keys of AirTags and other accessories are kept by the Find My app on a Mac: export them from the Mac, then import them here.

menu_options.json: One accessory or a list of keys (.json)
menu_options.key: A tag with a static key

archive.title: Import an export
archive.description: A zip of the exported Find My data: every accessory of its OwnedBeacons folder is added, with its name and key alignment when the zip has them.

plist.title: One accessory
plist.description: The accessory's file from OwnedBeacons and, optionally, its file from KeyAlignmentRecords, which makes the first fetch much faster for an accessory paired long ago.

data_description.name: Empty to use the model name

json.title: JSON file
json.description: An accessory exported as JSON, or a list of pre-generated private keys of a DIY tag.

key.title: Static key
key.description: A DIY tag that always broadcasts the same key.

error.invalid_plist: This file is not a property list (.plist).
error.encrypted_plist: This file is still encrypted (macOS 14 and later): export it with a tool that decrypts the Find My data.
error.not_an_accessory: This property list is not a Find My accessory.
error.invalid_zip: This file is not a zip of the Find My data.
error.no_accessory_in_zip: No accessory found: the zip should contain the OwnedBeacons folder.
error.invalid_json: This file is not an accessory or a list of keys.
error.invalid_key: This is not a private key (28 bytes, in base64 or hexadecimal).
error.upload_missing: The file was already read: choose the files again.

data_description.scan_interval: How often location reports are fetched (15 to 120 minutes). Accessories upload their position about every 15 minutes: asking more often brings nothing and risks Apple throttling the account.

data.locate: Ask the devices to locate themselves

data_description.scan_interval: How often iCloud is asked (2 to 60 minutes)
data_description.locate: Each refresh asks the devices for a fresh position, as the Find My app does. Off, the last position the devices sent on their own is read, which spares their battery.

icloud_only.message: {entity} is a Find My network accessory: only iCloud devices can ring, show a message or turn on Lost Mode.

refresh_too_soon.message: The last refresh was less than {seconds} seconds ago.

entry_not_loaded.message: No loaded Find My account with the ID {entry}.

play_sound.name: Play sound
play_sound.description: Makes an iCloud device ring, even on silent.

subject.name: Subject
subject.description: Title of the alert shown on the device.

display_message.name: Display message
display_message.description: Shows a message on the screen of an iCloud device.

lost_mode.name: Lost mode
lost_mode.description: Turns on Lost Mode on an iCloud device: it locks and shows the message and a number to call.

phone_number.name: Phone number
phone_number.description: Number the finder can call from the locked device.

message.name: Message
message.description: Text shown on the locked device (Apple's default text when empty).

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Fetches the positions now instead of waiting for the next refresh.

config_entry_id.name: Account
config_entry_id.description: Only this account (every account when empty).
